background_cache_diagnostic.timing_scope: Model duration includes the whole local driver attempt and HTTP/stream processing, not remote generation alone; no queue/prefill/network split.

background_cache_diagnostic.limits: Different implementations and requests, one sample each. No payload-prefix fingerprint or phase-level queue/network/prefill timings. Do not blame only the provider or claim cache optimization.
background_cache_diagnostic.final_ordinary_cache_relation: Provider-reported zero cached tokens and long first delta occur in the same ordinary-chat call. This is an association, not a controlled KV-cache causal result or an optimization gain.
cache_progression_findings: Final background admission reports cached counts 0, 8448 and 9728 across its three parent calls.
The following ordinary conversation call reports zero, while both later result-query calls and both restart-query calls report positive cached counts. Zero is not a property of the whole final run.
The final result-query second call reports 11776 cached tokens out of 13531 inputs, yet its first delta takes 11529.254 milliseconds. A positive cache count alone does not guarantee low latency.
The intermediate admission second call has no recorded first-delta timestamp; null must not be treated as zero or replaced with its full duration.
The final ordinary-chat zero-cache report and long first-delta delay are associated observations, not an identical-request comparison or proof of a KV-cache optimization benefit.

limits: The sixteen-second ordinary-chat slow sample was not reproduced by these five observations, and remains valid evidence.
The user instruction may repeat, but history and live context grow; complete requests are not identical.
Common-prefix counts refer to canonicalized serialized message characters, not tokenizer prefix lengths or direct KV-cache measurements. The Trace compares prior requests with matching settings.
A zero prefix count in the first row of each Trace instance means no prior request in that observer, not proof of no reusable prefix at the provider.
No unchanged-request randomized cold/warm control, provider queue attribution, production latency distribution or optimization gain is established.

The first timed turn reports 26 output tokens while its independently checked visible answer has two characters and the expected strict numeric form. Provider usage counts must not be treated as visible character counts or evidence of a formatting failure.
